podcast.body: The centerpiece of their 1967 LP "Days of Future Past," this nearly six-minute ballad with a poetry interlude was initially too long for pop radio. A severely edited three-minute version issued as a single in early 1968 flopped on the pop chart at number 103, but the song remained popular on progressive FM rock radio. In 1972, Decker Records issued a more judicious four-and-a-half-minute edit. By then, radio programmers and record buyers were accustomed to progressive and psychedelic pop sounds, leading "White Satin" to blow up on Top 40 radio and reach number two in November 1972, effectively defining The Moody Blues' career. "White Satin blew up on top 40 radio scaling the hot 100 and reaching number two in November 72."
